text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU memory OOM spike detected in pool-gpu-42 during prefill phase. 72 container restarts in 3m. Pager routed to @oncall-amber

oncall-amber: Ack. I'm on it — pulling logs now. tagging SRE.

sre-roma: On call. Which model and route? any customer-facing errors?

oncall-amber: Model: rwd-large-v1 (context 128k in some requests). Route: /v1/chat/stream-prod. We have repeated `prefill` failures and kernel restarts. Customers seeing stream dropouts.

engineer-lee: grabbing a trace from the node: `nvidia-smi`: GPU mem oscillating 15.6/16GB then process killed. Kernel shows `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in logs.

eng-runtime-ash: That matches a known long-prefill path where KV cache allocation + long prefix hits frag. Can we temporarily cap max_context on the route?

oncall-amber: I'm going to push a traffic rule to set `max_context_tokens=8192` (was 65536) and apply a per-route prefill token cap. Doing it now.

infra-liz: Heads up: reducing context will route some sessions to fallback smaller-model variant; that may increase latency but reduce OOMs.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: policy-change applied to /v1/chat/stream-prod: set max_context_tokens=8192, prefill_token_limit=4096 by oncall-amber.

engineer-lee: After the cap, container restarts dropped from 72->4 in the last 2m. Prefill OOM logs stopped.

cust-ops-jules: Customer impact: saw increased 503s on streaming for ~3m window. Top affected customers: acme-inc, lexor-ai, tutorly. Notified via high-priority email and follow-up in support tickets.

eng-runtime-ash: Recommend enabling aggressive KV trimming and dropping `prefetch_on_startup` for rwd-large-v1 until we patch allocator. Patch ready to hotpatch flag `--kvcache-trim=aggressive`.

sre-roma: Can you hotpatch a subset (canary) of nodes in pool-gpu-42? We'll watch stability then roll.

eng-runtime-ash: Doing canary now on nodes gpu-42-{03..05}. Command: ```kubectl set env daemonset/inference-runtime -n prod KVCACHE_TRIM=aggressive --record``` Monitoring logs.

engineer-lee: Logs from canary show fewer allocations during prefill, no CUDA illegal address. Good sign.

infra-liz: Also applied a temporary circuit-breaker at the gateway to shed >1 concurrent prefill per user to avoid thundering long prompts.

oncall-amber: After all mitigations: container restarts in pool-gpu-42 have flattened to 0 in 10m. Error rate on /v1/chat/stream-prod back to baseline.

cust-ops-jules: Customer update sent: we applied throttling and temporary model routing; no data exposure. Offering free credits for the impacted window.

eng-runtime-ash: Next steps: roll kvcache-trim to the rest of pool, push allocator fix (PR #1892) with improved prefill guardrails, and add a runtime alert to detect prefill allocation > 8GB in 500ms window.

sre-roma: I'll own immediate follow-up and RCA. Oncall-amber, please paste exact commands you used for the traffic rule so we can record in the postmortem.

oncall-amber: Traffic rule diff: ```- /v1/chat/stream-prod: no limits
+ /v1/chat/stream-prod: max_context_tokens=8192, prefill_token_limit=4096, concurrency_prefill_per_user=1```

engineer-lee: Captured kernel stacktrace snippet for the incident: ```I 03:12:45 cuda: illegal address at 0x7ffdead00000
I 03:12:45 container: oom-kill invoked, pid=23456
I 03:12:46 kubelet: restarting container inference-runtime-abc123```

cust-ops-jules: Logged affected request ids & sent to customers. No SLA credits yet — awaiting final impact calc.

eng-runtime-ash: PR will include a test harness for long-context prefill to reproduce locally. Once merged, we'll schedule a controlled rollout.

sre-roma: Good. Assigning postmortem owner: @sre-roma. Timeline: incident start 5151515151, mitigation applied 5151515170, stable 5151515210. We'll draft a one-pager and include follow-up action items.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, lead=@sre-roma.

oncall-amber: Thanks team. I'll keep the rule in place for 24h and then relax if metrics stay healthy. :thumbsup:

cust-ops-jules: I'll follow up with the three customers tomorrow with a summary and next steps.

eng-runtime-ash: Note for postmortem: consider infra limit protection for oversized prefill tokens at the edge to avoid serving runtime stress.

sre-roma: Closing thread after doc draft. Great response — low customer impact once mitigations hit.
